_note: Test fixture written by hand to exercise validation, ranking, dedupe and the verifier. Not model output and not used by the app.

questions.question: NRR went from 118% to 109% in two quarters while GRR held at 91%. That's an expansion problem, not churn. Which segment stopped expanding, and what has to be true to get NRR back to 118%?
questions.why_they_ask: Expansion was the engine of the growth case; she needs to know if it's fixable.
answer_outline: Headline: the drop is mid-market expansion, not churn.
Evidence: NRR 118% to 109% since Q1 2026; GRR steady at 91%.
Action: name the segment plan and the quarter we expect NRR to turn.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Blaming the market when GRR held steady and churn is not the problem.

questions.question: Expansion slowed and NRR is down 9 points since Q1 2026. Is it the product or the pricing?
questions.why_they_ask: Wants to know the root cause of the expansion slowdown.
answer_outline: Headline: it is the mid-market seat-expansion motion.
Evidence: NRR fell 9 pts in two quarters to 109%.
Action: the packaging change we are testing.

questions.question: Pipeline coverage for next quarter is 2.4x against a 3x target. Why should we believe next quarter's number?
questions.why_they_ask: Thin pipeline after two misses means a third miss is likely.
answer_outline: Headline: coverage is 80% of target and we have sized the gap.
Evidence: 2.4x vs 3x; net new ARR $2.87M vs $3.8M plan in Q3.
Action: the pipeline we are adding and a reset plan if it doesn't land.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Promising the number without showing where the missing pipeline comes from.

questions.question: Enterprise logos are up 40% year over year, from 30 to 42. Is this a real motion we should fund harder, or a handful of lucky deals?
questions.why_they_ask: The one bright spot could be the next growth engine.
answer_outline: Headline: enterprise is working and repeatable.
Evidence: 42 enterprise logos vs 30 a year ago (+40%).
Action: the specific investment we propose and its payback.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Overselling enterprise to distract from the NRR decline.

questions.question: How is the business doing overall?
answer_outline: a
b
c

questions.question: You missed net new ARR plan by 20.5% in Q2 and 24.5% in Q3. What changed in how you build the forecast, and why should we believe this one?
questions.why_they_ask: Two material misses in a row are a credibility problem, not a sales problem.
answer_outline: Headline: we own the miss and changed the forecast method.
Evidence: $3.1M vs $3.9M plan in Q2, $2.87M vs $3.8M in Q3.
Action: the new pipeline-weighted forecast and who signs off on it.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Explaining each miss as a one-off slipped deal.

questions.question: Gross margin is 72.8%, down 3 points from 75.8% a year ago, and cost of revenue ran 10.1% over budget. Is the hosting cost from the migration temporary or structural?
questions.why_they_ask: A permanent margin reset changes the valuation story.
answer_outline: Headline: most of it is migration overlap, with a dated plan to remove it.
Evidence: margin 72.8% vs 75.8%; cost of revenue $3.17M vs $2.88M budget.
Action: the hosting milestones and the margin we expect when they land.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Calling it temporary without a date and an owner.

questions.question: Revenue came in at $11.64M against a $12M budget while opex landed on budget. Did anyone see the revenue shortfall coming before quarter end?
questions.why_they_ask: Tests whether management has early-warning visibility.
answer_outline: Headline: we saw it in week 8 and should have flagged it sooner.
Evidence: revenue $11.64M vs $12M budget (-3%); opex $14.1M on budget.
Action: the in-quarter flash report the board will now receive.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Claiming you saw it coming but didn't tell the board.

questions.question: Runway fell from 22 to 17 months in two quarters. When does the board need to see a financing plan?
questions.why_they_ask: Governance: the board must not be surprised by a raise.
answer_outline: Headline: we will bring options by next meeting.
Evidence: 17 months of runway on $34.17M cash.
Action: the decision timeline.

questions.question: Is your plan to bring NRR back to 125% realistic?
answer_outline: Headline: yes.
Evidence: NRR was 125% last year.
Action: hire more CSMs.

questions.question: At a 2.1x burn multiple and 17 months of runway, when do you need to raise, and on what story?
questions.why_they_ask: He has to decide whether to lead an inside round or push for cuts.
answer_outline: Headline: we plan to raise from strength, with a recovery story.
Evidence: burn multiple 2.1x vs 1.5x a year ago; 17 months of runway.
Action: the two levers that get burn multiple back under 2x before we raise.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Saying 17 months is plenty of time.

questions.question: Net burn is flat at about $6M a quarter but net new ARR fell to $2.87M. Which spend isn't producing growth anymore?
questions.why_they_ask: Flat burn with falling growth means efficiency, not spend, is the problem.
answer_outline: Headline: the efficiency drop is growth, not spend.
Evidence: net burn $6.03M; net new ARR $2.87M vs $4.2M a year ago.
Action: where we cut or redeploy to raise net new ARR per dollar.
questions.trap_to_avoid: Proposing across-the-board cuts that hit the enterprise motion.

questions.question: With burn multiple at 2.1x and pipeline at 2.4x coverage, what's the downside case for runway if next quarter misses again?
questions.why_they_ask: Wants the downside before it happens.
answer_outline: Headline: we have a downside plan.
Evidence: 17 months runway; 2.4x coverage vs 3x target.
Action: the trigger point for cost actions.

questions.question: Enterprise logos grew 40%. Can enterprise deals carry the raise story?
answer_outline: Headline: enterprise is the story.
Evidence: 42 logos, +40%.
Action: show cohort data.

questions.question: At 2.1x burn and 17 months of runway, when exactly do you need to raise and on what story?
questions.why_they_ask: Duplicate on purpose to test dedupe.
answer_outline: a 2.1x
b 17 months
c
